name: TX-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Fallon with large financial advantage
Democrat Pearce raised only $16k with minimal cash
model.rationale: Fallon holds a heavily Republican seat, a dominant fundraising edge, and markets price him near certain; Pearce's negligible war chest gives no sign of competitiveness.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major outside spending against Fallon could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pat Fallon seeks reelection in a northeast Texas district that leans about twelve points Republican at the presidential level. He enters the general election as a well-funded incumbent, with roughly $1.1 million on hand and modest outside support, after easily securing renomination.

Democratic challenger Jason Pearce has raised only about $16,000 and holds minimal cash, with no outside spending on either side and no public polling of the race. Prediction markets give Fallon roughly a 94% chance of winning. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture makes this seat safely Republican, with little evidence suggesting a competitive contest.
